blocks.etymology: From Middle English tagge (“small piece hanging from a garment”), probably of North Germanic origin. Compare Norwegian tagg (“point; prong; barb; tag”), Swedish tagg (“thorn; prickle; tine”), Icelandic tág (“a willow-twig”). Compare also tack.

senses.definition: To link a person's username to an image or message online.

examples.en: Don't forget to tag me in the party photos.
examples.vi: Đừng quên gắn thẻ tôi vào những bức ảnh bữa tiệc nhé.

senses.definition: To fix a label to an object to show its price or details.

senses.definition: To touch another person during a game of tag.

examples.en: Tom ran fast and tagged his brother.
examples.vi: Tom chạy thật nhanh và chạm vào người em trai mình.

senses.definition: To mark digital information or files with keywords to organize them.

examples.en: I spent hours tagging my music files by genre.
examples.vi: Tôi đã dành hàng giờ để gắn thẻ các tệp nhạc theo thể loại.

senses.definition: To go somewhere with other people, especially when not asked.

To affix a label to (potentially dangerous machinery) to indicate why it has been shut down. To avoid accidents, only the person who affixed the label is authorized to remove it and restart the machinery.

Of a baserunner, when a fly ball is hit, to put one's foot on the base one is currently at until the ball is caught. When the ball is caught, the baserunner may attempt to advance to the next base, at the risk of being tagged out.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English tiren, tirien, teorien, from Old English tȳrian, tēorian (“to fail, cease, become weary, be tired, exhausted; tire, weary, exhaust”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from Proto-West Germanic *teuʀōn (“to cease”), which is possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dews- (“to fail, be behind, lag”). Compare Ancient Greek δεύομαι (deúomai, “to lack”), Sanskrit दोष (dóṣa, “crime, fault, vice, deficiency”).
